citedMandateClauses: 4. Vote for security fixes, audits, bug bounties, emergency patches, key rotations and upgrades that reduce trust in any single party.
7. Vote against proposals that add new privileged roles, multisigs or upgrade powers, or that weaken timelocks or voting rules.
10. Abstain when ... its on-chain actions cannot be matched to its description.
rationale: The proposal recalls about 12.5M UNI from eight Franchiser delegations back to the Governance Timelock. It is a return of treasury-owned tokens, not a transfer, grant, or new commitment out of the treasury, so the spending limits in rule 1 do not apply. It adds no new privileged roles, multisigs, or upgrade powers, and does not weaken timelocks or voting rules, so rule 7 is not triggered. It reduces concentration of voting power held by third-party delegates, which fits the mandate's priority on reducing trust in any single party (rule 4) and its aim that the protocol survive. Against that, returning tokens to the timelock is not itself a security fix or a direct return of value to holders, and the proposal's on-chain action is a single recallMany call whose calldata is truncated in the summary, so matching it fully to the description is not verified. Those uncertainties keep confidence moderate.
